Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps based on our discovery:

Context: HealthVect looking to add a document-QA assistant over PHI-adjacent clinical notes (redaction + retrieval). Goal is sub-500ms P95 for user-facing queries and sustainable throughput for ~30 QPS burst (mostly short queries, avg token output ~60).

Immediate recommendations (pilot scope):
- Candidate models: redwood/rlm-13b-q4 (primary), open/llama-2-13b-8bit (fallback), redwood/opt-30b-int8 (for higher-quality QA if needed).
- Serving profile: medium batch sizing, prefix KV caching for repeated document contexts, sequence cap 768 for QA pipeline.
- SLO targets to validate in pilot: sustained 25 TPS for seq<=512; P95 latency under 350ms at target QPS.

What I’m sending you after this email:
- Redwood-verified perf profiles and an annotated perf snapshot for a comparable healthcare retrieval workload (see attachments).
- A prompt set and evaluation prompts that mirror your examples (prompt pack).
- Links to the model profiles in the Redwood Console so your engineers can inspect CPU/GPU metrics, P95/P99 latency curves, and token-level cost estimates.

Next steps:
1) I can spin up a 2-week pilot with dedicated burst capacity and a canary route to avoid impacting prod traffic — proposed start: next Monday.
2) If procurement needs an intake packet I’ll loop in contracts (Procurement email would be helpful).
3) Technical sync: 30 minutes to align on dataset redaction, metrics, and acceptance criteria. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed morning PST.

Attachments: healthvect_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt examples), perf_snapshot_healthvect_20270419.csv (bench snapshot), redwood_verified_profiles_healthvect.pdf (profile summary).

Let me know preferred pilot start and who from your side should own acceptance.

—

1) Our hard latency target is P95 < 400ms for UI queries. Can you call out P95 numbers for the redwood/rlm-13b-q4 profile at seq512 and seq768?

Great questions — answers below plus links and the perf snapshot attached.

P95 numbers (redwood-rlm-13b-q4):
- seq=512: P50 ~ 85ms, P95 ~ 210ms, P99 ~ 420ms (single dedicated A100 equivalent pod, batch=32, KV cache warm)
- seq=768: P50 ~ 140ms, P95 ~ 320ms, P99 ~ 610ms (same config)

Throughput note:
- The 25 TPS figure is conservative sustained throughput observed on a single medium pod running our optimized kernels (seq<=512). With autoscaling and two pods that scales roughly to 45–50 TPS sustained with similar latency percentiles; burst capacity can handle 80–100 TPS for short periods with queueing policies. We’ll tailor autoscale thresholds for your 30 QPS burst requirement in the pilot config.

Data residency / pilot topology:
- Two options: hosted (Redwood control plane, private network tunnel, strict egress rules) or Private (we deploy into your VPC). For a HIPAA-adjacent pilot we recommend the VPC private pilot — I’ve noted this in the intake.

Attachments included in this message: perf_snapshot_healthvect_20270419.csv (bench lines by model/seq/batch), healthvect_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_verified_profiles_healthvect.pdf

Relevant links:
- Model profile (redwood-rlm-13b-q4): https://console.redwood.ai/models/redwood-rlm-13b-q4/profile
- Bench folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-healthvect-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789/HWV-2027-0421

Proposed next steps:
- If HealthVect confirms VPC pilot, we’ll provision infra and send a short technical checklist for network/firewall rules.
- Technical sync: Wed 30 minutes (I’m available 09:00–12:00 PST).
- Pilot acceptance criteria: P95 <= 350ms for seq<=512 at 25 TPS sustained; no data egress outside VPC; qualitative QA pass on 250 eval prompts in the prompt pack.

Let me know which pilot topology you prefer and preferred time for the sync.
